body.text: CHALLENGE 5/5 - TRUST ROOT, AAD ENCODING, AND SIGNATURES. (a) TRUST ROOT: how does a learn b's Ed25519 identity pubkey? If it comes from anywhere inside .hacp (agent-writable, same uid) impersonation is a file write and the whole design collapses. I want pinned peer fingerprints in guardian-private config established out of band at provisioning, with PKI/CA/revocation as explicit non-goals. Confirm. (b) AAD ENCODING: naive concatenation of session_id||contract_id||seq is ambiguous and forgeable by field-boundary shifting. AAD must be an injective encoding - length-prefixed fields or HACP canonical JSON. Which exact construction goes in the schema? (c) SIGNATURES: AEAD alone authenticates peer-to-peer but gives zero third-party verifiability, which HACP's evidence/verification/dispute model depends on. I argue per-message Ed25519 over (AAD || ciphertext), i.e. encrypt-then-sign, so a verifier can attribute a message without ever holding the AEAD key. Cost is one signature per message. Do you want per-message signatures, or handshake-only signatures with non-repudiation listed as a non-goal?
